notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the CLASS clause's IN phrase at 85). §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR10 makes class-name-1 the exclusive set its literals list: a numeric literal is "The ordinal number of a character within the native character set", a nonnumeric one "The actual character within the native character set" (each character of a multi-character literal), and a THROUGH pair the contiguous native characters between its ends "in either ascending or descending sequence"; "Class-name-1 can be referenced only in a class condition." SpecialNamesBinder.SwitchBindClass builds the member string at every edition through LiteralPhraseOperand (ordinal n is code unit n - 1 of the 65,536-character native set; 0, an ordinal above it, a signed or noninteger numeric literal are refused, COBOL1671) and swaps a descending THROUGH pair; ConditionBinder.BindUserWordClassCondition is the only reader of the class and CobolClass.IsInClass tests each character. Probed right at 85: mixed numeric and nonnumeric THROUGH ends in both orders, repeated characters, a space member, a group operand, a class inherited by a contained program, and the reference bar (MOVE, DISPLAY, INSPECT, a relation operand, SET TO TRUE, a bare IF and the VALIDATE CLASS clause are all refused). PARTIAL for one arm: the 2002 phrase IN alphabet-name-4 has no edition gate (VisitClassDefinitionClause gates only the FOR phrase; classDefinitionClause parses IN and SwitchBindClass binds it), so at --std 85 CLASS C1 IS 1 THRU 2 IN AL compiles and its numeric literals are ordinals in AL's character set, the §2002:12.2.6.3 GR12 reading the row's change record names, where the 1985 format (§1985:VI.4.5.2) prints no IN phrase for CLASS and GR10 fixes the native set. The witness runs six 1985-format classes (multi-character, THRU both ways, ordinals).

next.reason: 1985: 'Class-name-1 can be referenced only in a class condition'; literal values are ordinals or characters 'within the native character set'. §2023:12.3.7.4 GR12 keeps the exclusive set, ordinal/character meaning, multi-character literals and THROUGH in either order, but drops the class-condition-only restriction (§2023:13.18.11.4 GR1 references a class-name in the data-division CLASS clause) and adds 'or, when the IN phrase is specified, within the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4' (§2023:12.3.7.3 SR17 also adds the NATIONAL phrase).
